long_biography.plain_text:
COGEMAD reflects Emad Khashoggi's attempt to treat luxury property development as a single design-and-delivery discipline. He founded the company in Cannes in 1989, two years after graduating from Pepperdine University. Its first work transformed a Belle Époque villa, and later projects extended the model to apartment developments, historic restorations and newly built estates in France and other European markets.

Khashoggi's approach joins architects, engineers, interior designers and specialist craftspeople within one operation. Château Louis XIV became the clearest expression of that method: a newly constructed residence shaped by seventeenth-century French architecture but equipped with modern systems. The project moved COGEMAD onto the international luxury-property stage, while Khashoggi has remained its founder and chief executive. His father had already worked in property development, giving him a relevant family platform before he created the separate business.
